text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.84% today, recovering modestly after a sharp 3.8% drop on November 18th. The rebound comes as oil prices stabilized—US crude holding at $89.53 per barrel and world oil at $92.94—following concerns about Middle Eastern supply disruptions and tightening European energy markets. The stock has found a floor around $134–$136 after falling from $142 just a week ago, suggesting some stabilization in investor sentiment.

The underlying driver for the week's volatility appears rooted in geopolitical risk: the Iran conflict has damaged confidence in the Strait of Hormuz as a reliable shipping route for oil, raising questions about future supply reliability. Meanwhile, emerging pressure on energy infrastructure—from Europe's depleted gas stocks facing cold weather, to surging data center electricity demands—creates longer-term tailwinds for traditional energy producers, even if near-term market swings remain volatile.
